Pareeksha v1.0.0: voice-agent QA for Indian-language calls. It runs simulated callers over real Gnani speech and a phone-line simulator, has an LLM judge score each call against a versioned rubric, and runs everything through Kafka workers with retries, a DLQ and idempotent CRM delivery.

What's in this release
- Simulated callers (Pipecat) with personas, noise and PSTN profiles, and a mock EMI agent with 5 planted bugs.
- LLM judge (DeepSeek by default) with rubric `rubric-2026-10-v1` and turn-cited findings.
- Audits of real recordings through an inbound webhook; HubSpot notes and signed webhook sinks.
- Dialect ASR gap report: Kannada (Old Mysore, North Karnataka, Coastal, Bengaluru code-mix) and Hindi, from the Vaani dataset (CC-BY-4.0).
- Pluggable speech providers: Gnani (default), Google, Azure, ElevenLabs, Deepgram.
- Web app, Python SDK and CLI, and a GitHub Action regression gate.

Known open items (see STATUS.md and proof/)
- Judge calibration against owner labels on 30 calls: kappa 0.19, below the 0.6 target. Rubric v2 (penalising replies that ignore the caller) is in progress.
- Demo video and launch post are not published yet.
